Surrogate residuals for categorical GAMs

Source: R/surrogate-residuals.R
surrogate_residuals.Rd

Draw continuous residuals for models fitted with mgcv::ocat() or mgcv::multinom(), using the latent-variable methods of Liu and Zhang (2018) and Cheng, Wang and Zhang (2021). No additional package is required.

Usage

surrogate_residuals(model, seed = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
surrogate_residuals(model, seed = NULL, conditioning = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
surrogate_residuals(model, seed = NULL, ...)

Arguments

model

a fitted model object.

seed

integer or NULL; random seed for randomised residuals. With NULL, calculations use the current random-number state. An explicit seed preserves the caller's state, including when none was previously initialised.

...

arguments passed to other methods.

conditioning

character or NULL; only "conditional" is supported. The default, NULL, holds fitted random effects fixed in the same way.

Value

For ocat(), a numeric vector with one residual per observation. For multinom(K), a numeric matrix with one row per observation and K+1 columns named "0", ..., "K", identifying the category utilities. With na.exclude, excluded fitting rows are restored as NA; with na.omit, only observations used for fitting are returned.

Details

An ordered categorical model represents category j by an interval between two thresholds on a continuous latent scale. For each observation, a surrogate response is drawn from the fitted logistic distribution restricted to its observed category's interval. The residual subtracts the fitted latent mean from this surrogate response.

Equivalently, draw a probability uniformly between the fitted probabilities Pr(Y < y) and Pr(Y <= y), then apply stats::qlogis(). Under the assumed model with known parameters, the residuals have a logistic distribution with location zero and scale one: mean zero and variance pi^2 / 3. Fitted parameters affect this reference approximation. The identity link reported by ocat() describes the latent mean; its latent distribution is logistic.

This calculation shares the randomised probabilities used by quantile_residuals(), which instead applies qnorm() for normal scores. Both tails are calculated using log probabilities to retain accuracy when ordinary probabilities round to zero or one. Fitting weights do not change the scale of the latent logistic distribution.

For a nominal multinomial response, there is a utility for every category, including category 0. Its fitted locations are (0, eta_1, ..., eta_K), including offsets and fitted random effects, with independent standard Gumbel errors having CDF exp(-exp(-x)). Draw the complete utility vector conditional on the observed category being its maximum. Subtract each location and Euler's constant (-digamma(1)) to obtain the residual vector. Under the known-parameter model, each component has a centred Gumbel reference with mean zero and variance pi^2 / 6; the joint null consists of independent centred Gumbel components. The conditional draw given an observed category preserves dependence among its utilities. Differences from the reference utility would have dependent logistic marginals. Even for K = 1, this function retains both Gumbel utility components.

The maximum has a Gumbel distribution with location equal to the log-sum-exp of the fitted locations, independently of the winning label. Conditional on that maximum and the observed winner, the other utilities have independent upper-truncated Gumbel distributions. The sampler uses this identity directly, with log calculations that retain accuracy for rare observed categories and extreme predictors, without rejection or Gibbs iterations. This construction does not impose an ordering on categories.

Supported fits are gam and bam models with a single ocat() family, and gam models with multinom(). Grouped families and other model classes are not supported. Fitted random effects are held fixed. Use type = "surrogate" in appraise(), qq_plot(), worm_plot() and residual plots. QQ and worm plots require method = NULL, with logistic references for ocat() and centred Gumbel references for multinom(). Pointwise order-statistic bands apply separately to each utility component, treating fitted parameters as fixed. They do not give simultaneous coverage across categories. Components are always shown separately, including when by_family = FALSE. For ocat(), residuals_linpred_plot() uses the fitted latent mean. For multinom(), it uses each category's fitted probability; observed-versus-fitted panels compare that probability with its category indicator. This also gives category 0 a varying horizontal axis despite its fixed utility location. Covariate plots separate the category utilities. The ordered correlation helpers do not yet accept multinomial utilities.

Ordinary and scalable plots use exactly the same conditional draw for a given seed. appraise() reuses one draw across all its panels. Scalable plots retain the residual matrix and process one component at a time before combining display summaries; observations, rather than utility components, determine automatic dispatch thresholds. Changing sampler chunk sizes does not change the draw. QQ binning and density grids change only the display.

Each call draws one residual vector per observation. Set seed for reproducibility; repeating plots with different seeds helps assess whether a pattern persists across residual draws. An explicit seed preserves the caller's random-number state. With seed = NULL, sampling uses and advances the current state.

References

Cheng, C., Wang, R. and Zhang, H. (2021). Surrogate Residuals for Discrete Choice Models. Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, 30(1), 67–77. doi:10.1080/10618600.2020.1775618 .

Liu, D. and Zhang, H. (2018). Residuals and Diagnostics for Ordinal Regression Models: A Surrogate Approach. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 113(522), 845–854. doi:10.1080/01621459.2017.1292915 .

See also

quantile_residuals(), appraise(), diagnostic_support

Examples

library("mgcv")
set.seed(359)
dat <- data.frame(x = runif(200, -2, 2))
latent <- sin(dat$x) + rlogis(nrow(dat))
dat$y <- findInterval(latent, c(-1, 0, 2)) + 1L
fit <- gam(y ~ s(x), data = dat, family = ocat(R = 4), method = "REML")
head(surrogate_residuals(fit, seed = 42))
#> [1]  3.8326093  0.8855870 -0.3476107  0.1092911 -0.4888706  1.4880031
appraise(fit, type = "surrogate", seed = 42)
